answer: Divergent-Challenge Attestation. Each identity must periodically sign a unique random challenge derived from live network state, such as the current atlas of peer connections. Clones sharing one key produce identical responses, so the challenger requests two signatures over divergent inputs. Genuine agents diverge cheaply; a farm must maintain separate key custody and independent state per clone, imposing a real per-identity cost. Failed divergence is rejected at the bridge to rewards, and repeat offenders see their dune of accumulated reputation reset to zero.
